question: A science textbook shows the magnetic field lines around two bar magnets labelled A and B. In A, six lines enter its south pole, and in B, three lines emerge from its north pole. The strength of A is □( ), the strength of B is □( ).
solution:
The correct answer is __**double**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The magnetic field strength is directly proportional to the number of magnetic field lines.
 
• In magnet A, six magnetic field lines enter its south pole.
 
• In magnet B, three magnetic field lines emerge from its north pole.
 
• Since magnet A has twice the number of magnetic field lines compared to magnet B, the strength of magnet A is double that of magnet B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic Field Lines**

 
 
• Magnetic field lines are a visual representation of the magnetic field around a magnet.
 
• They emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole of a magnet.
 
• The density of the magnetic field lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field Strength**
 
 
• The strength of a magnetic field is a measure of the force exerted by the magnetic field.
 
• It is proportional to the number of field lines passing through a given area.
 
• Magnetic field strength is measured in units called Tesla (T) or Gauss (G).
 
 
 
• **Bar Magnets**
 
 
• A bar magnet is a rectangular piece of an object, made up of iron, steel, or any other ferromagnetic substance, that shows permanent magnetic properties.
 
• Bar magnets have two poles: a north pole and a south pole.
 
• When suspended freely, a bar magnet aligns itself with the earth's magnetic field, with its north pole pointing towards the earth's geographic north.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Poles**
 
 
• The two ends of a magnet where the magnetic force is strongest are called poles.
 
• Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole.
 
• Like poles repel each other, while unlike poles attract each other.
